prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a supermarket checkout layout with a stainless-steel counter extending diagonally from the bottom-center foreground (~0.3–1.2 m away) toward the upper center, flanked by a red shopping cart and white reusable bags on the lower left (~0.2–0.8 m) and a vertical partition on the left of the counter (~0.4–1.0 m), while store aisles and potted plants recede into the dark background (>3 m). On the right side of the counter, a cashier in a red shirt stands roughly 0.8–1.5 m from the camera wearer and 0.3–0.6 m from the counter's groceries and card terminal, facing left/downward toward the counter rather than looking at the camera wearer, with their lower body occluded by the counter and their head/torso partly cropped out of the right frame edge in frames 2, 3, and 5. Across the five frames, the cashier leans forward and extends both arms leftward into the ~0.6–1.0 m range to reach the blue-lidded tubs and packages on the counter, while the camera wearer's own left or right hand enters the bottom foreground (~0.3–0.5 m) within arm's reach of the groceries in frames 2, 3, 4, and 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the foreground bags and cart handle from the mid-ground counter surface and shows the continuous planar recession of the conveyor area. However, the map is unreliable on the transparent upper section of the checkout partition—which it renders as an opaque, bright near surface in frames 2–5—leaving the distance of the background shelves behind the glass distorted and merging clustered small groceries into indistinct blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the cashier (`person`) on the right side of the checkout counter (~0.8–1.5 m from the camera wearer) and the card terminal (`cell phone`, ~0.9–1.1 m away and ~0.3–0.5 m to the cashier's left), along with sporadic detections of the camera wearer's foreground hand (`person`, ~0.3–0.5 m at the bottom center in frame 2) and a few counter items (`bowl`, `cup` at ~0.6–0.8 m). In frame 1, it also segments two monitors above and behind the counter as `tv` (~1.2–2.0 m away, above the counter surface), while across frames 2 through 5 the cashier's mask shifts closer to the center as their arms extend leftward within arm's reach of the counter items and card terminal, with their torso partially out of view on the right in frames 2, 3, and 5. Unlike the cluttered RGB image, the segmentation masks provide sharp silhouette boundaries for the cashier's reaching arms and consistently track the position of the card terminal relative to the cashier's hands across frames 2–5. However, the map is highly unreliable for scene completeness and classification: it completely misses the shopping cart, bags, checkout counter, partition, and almost all grocery items, misclassifies the payment terminal as a `cell phone`, and fails to detect the camera wearer's visible hands in frames 3, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is largely empty across the sequence, detecting the cashier's yellow upper-body skeleton on the right side of the counter (~0.8–1.5 m away) only in frames 1 and 4, and a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom center (~0.4 m away, within arm's reach of the counter groceries) only in frame 5. In frame 1, the cashier's torso and shoulder keypoints are compact and angled toward the left-front (~1.2–1.5 m away), whereas in frame 4 the facial keypoints orient downward toward the counter (not looking at the camera wearer) and both arm skeletons extend ~0.4–0.5 m forward and leftward to place the wrists directly over the groceries at ~0.7–0.9 m from the camera wearer. The cashier's hips and legs remain unmapped because they are occluded below the counter edge, and the camera wearer's full body is behind the camera viewpoint. Where present, the skeleton map makes the 3D-projected joint articulation, shoulder tilt, and dual-arm extension of the cashier in frame 4—as well as the finger orientation of the wearer's reaching hand in frame 5—much easier to read than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. Nevertheless, the pose map is severely unreliable across time, suffering complete tracking dropouts for the cashier in frames 2, 3, and 5 when their head and torso are partially cropped at the right frame boundary, and missing the camera wearer's visible hands in frames 2, 3, and 4.
